title: Chemical Engineering and Artificial Intelligence, BSChE (Boston)
overview: The Boston BSChE combines chemical engineering with artificial intelligence methods for predictive models, process optimization and experimental design. The published degree requires 134 semester hours. The award is BSChE, retained as other in the normalized award enum.

outcomes.text: The program aims to apply AI to chemical-engineering prediction, process optimization and experimental design.

courses.name: Conservation Principles in Chemical Engineering
courses.description: Uses conservation laws to calculate material and energy balances in chemical processes.
courses.prerequisites: CHEM 1151 with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 233M with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 1161 with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 1211 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: CHME 2308 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Mass/energy balance and chemical-process analysis are chemical-engineering domain practice, not mathematical theory merely because calculations are used.

courses.name: Transport Processes 1
courses.description: Studies fluid and energy transport for analysis of industrial engineering processes.
courses.prerequisites: ( MATH 2321 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 316M with a minimum grade of D- ); CHME 2308 with a minimum grade of D- ; ( MATH 2341 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 315M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- )

category_review.locator: CHME 2310 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The primary subject is physical fluid and energy transport in engineering processes; mathematical methods serve that domain.

courses.name: Engineering Thermodynamics
courses.description: Applies thermodynamics and real-fluid properties to batch and flow engineering systems.
courses.prerequisites: CHME 2308 with a minimum grade of D- ; ( MATH 2321 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 316M with a minimum grade of D- )

category_review.locator: CHME 2320 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Thermodynamic laws, properties and engineering systems are physical/engineering domain knowledge.

courses.name: Chemical Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Investigates transport principles through chemical-engineering experiments, emphasizing safe experimental design and technical reporting.
courses.prerequisites: CHME 2310 with a minimum grade of D- ; ( CHME 2320 with a minimum grade of D- or CHME 2322 with a minimum grade of D- ); ( ENGW 3302 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or ENGW 3315 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- )

category_review.locator: CHME 3305 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course is a chemical-engineering laboratory centered on transport experiments and design; communication supports the domain practice.

courses.name: Recitation for CHME 3305
courses.description: Supports the chemical-engineering laboratory through safety, experimental design, data analysis and reporting.

category_review.locator: CHME 3306 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The explicit accompanying CHME 3305 laboratory context establishes engineering experimental practice; zero hours do not erase the separate required recitation identity.

courses.name: Transport Processes 2
courses.description: Studies coupled energy and mass transport and its applications to engineering processes.
courses.prerequisites: CHME 2310 with a minimum grade of D- ; ( MATH 2341 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 315M with a minimum grade of D- )

category_review.locator: CHME 3312 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Physical transport phenomena in industrial engineering processes are the substantive domain.

courses.name: Chemical Thermodynamics
courses.description: Analyzes mixture properties, phase behavior and equilibrium in chemical reactions.
courses.prerequisites: CHME 2320 with a minimum grade of D- or CHME 2322 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: CHME 3322 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Chemical mixture thermodynamics and reaction equilibria are scientific/engineering domain content.

courses.name: Chemical Engineering Kinetics
courses.description: Uses reaction kinetics and experimental data to design chemical reactors.
courses.prerequisites: CHME 3312 with a minimum grade of D- ; CHME 3322 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: CHME 4510 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Reaction rates and reactor design establish chemical-engineering practice; data analysis is a supporting method.

courses.name: Chemical Engineering Process Control
courses.description: Models chemical-process dynamics and designs feedback, feed-forward and cascade controls.
courses.prerequisites: CHME 3312 with a minimum grade of D- ; CHME 3322 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: CHME 4512 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The description applies transforms, dynamic models and controller design to chemical-process variables. Control systems here are engineering domain content, not computing infrastructure or AI by name.

courses.name: Separations and Process Analysis
courses.description: Designs chemical processing systems using separation methods, simulations and economic evaluation.
courses.prerequisites: CHME 3312 with a minimum grade of D- ; CHME 3322 with a minimum grade of D- ; CHME 4510 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: CHME 4701 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Chemical process/separation design, operations and engineering economics are the domain; simulation use does not establish general software construction.

courses.name: Chemical Process Design Capstone
courses.description: Develops and validates a team chemical-process design using experiments or simulation, considering practical and societal constraints.
courses.prerequisites: ( CHME 3305 with a minimum grade of D- or CHME 4315 with a minimum grade of D- ); CHME 4701 with a minimum grade of D- ; ( CHME 4512 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or PHYS 3600 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- )

category_review.locator: CHME 4703 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The required capstone designs a chemical process and demonstrates feasibility; ethical/economic constraints and reports support the engineering design objective.

courses.name: Recitation for CHME 4703
courses.description: Provides shared lectures and guest presentations supporting the chemical-process design capstone.

category_review.locator: CHME 4705 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The source explicitly accompanies the chemical-process design capstone; its domain classification is based on that named course relationship rather than its recitation title alone.

courses.name: Cornerstone of Engineering 1
courses.description: Introduces engineering design and programming through projects, laboratories and an original design solution.

category_review.locator: GE 1501 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Hands-on engineering design and prototypes are the organizing domain practice; programming and graphics are supporting tools.

courses.name: Cornerstone of Engineering 2
courses.description: Continues project-based engineering design with analysis, programming, ethical reasoning and working prototypes.
courses.prerequisites: GE 1501 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or ENGR 150M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: GE 1502 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The course continues engineering analysis, design, modeling and prototype construction using software and ethical reasoning as tools.

courses.name: Discrete Structures
courses.description: Develops discrete structures, logic, proofs and counting methods for computing.

category_review.locator: CS 1800 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Sets, relations, induction, proof, logic and counting form discrete mathematical methods; computing motivates their use.

courses.name: Introduction to Program Design and Implementation
courses.description: Introduces programming, dataset analysis and ethical issues in software design.

category_review.locator: CS 2000 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The course teaches program construction, coding and introductory data processing to students without programming experience.

courses.name: Lab for CS 2000
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting introductory programming coursework.

category_review.locator: CS 2001 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The lab explicitly accompanies the introductory program-design course and practices its computing topics.

courses.name: Program Design and Implementation 1
courses.description: Develops program design, object-oriented abstractions and software engineering practices.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: CS 2100 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Data/object-oriented design, data structures, abstraction, testing and software construction are the central methods.

courses.name: Lab for CS 2100
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting program design coursework.

category_review.locator: CS 2101 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The lab explicitly accompanies the reviewed program-design and software-construction course.

courses.name: Introduction to Databases
courses.description: Develops relational database design, SQL and introductory database-system techniques.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or EECE 2560 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: CS 3200 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Relational database design, query processing, indexing, concurrency and recovery are database-system methods.

courses.name: Advanced Programming with Data
courses.description: Develops robust software architectures and data pipelines using substantial datasets.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 3500 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Software architectures, reusable APIs, testing and maintainable data pipelines center on general software design and implementation.

courses.name: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Studies the mathematical basis of AI through linear algebra, probability and computational exercises.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 3000 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The description explicitly emphasizes linear algebra, probability and numerical mathematical foundations, using AI as their motivating application.

courses.name: Information Presentation and Visualization
courses.description: Studies how to design, implement and evaluate visual representations of data.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2510 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 4200 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Visualization combines programming, perception, visual communication and domain presentation; the description does not establish one defensible primary category among these.

courses.name: Large-Scale Information Storage and Retrieval
courses.description: Studies scalable data storage, distributed databases and retrieval methods.
courses.prerequisites: ( CS 3100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 310M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 3500 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 3500 with a minimum grade of D- ); CS 3200 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: DS 4300 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Distributed databases, storage architectures, reliability and data retrieval are computing infrastructure methods.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.description: Introduces predictive modeling and major supervised and unsupervised learning methods.
courses.prerequisites: DS 3000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 250M with a minimum grade of D- or ( MATH 2331 with a minimum grade of D- ; MATH 3081 with a minimum grade of D- )

category_review.locator: DS 4400 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Supervised and unsupervised learning, predictive models, model evaluation and learning algorithms are the explicit central content.

courses.name: General Chemistry for Engineers
courses.description: Introduces matter, reactions, thermodynamics, equilibrium and electrochemistry for engineering.

category_review.locator: CHEM 1151 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: States of matter, chemical bonding, thermodynamics, equilibrium and electrochemistry are chemical-science domain content.

courses.name: Recitation for CHEM 1151
courses.description: Provides guided discussion and practice for engineering chemistry.

category_review.locator: CHEM 1153 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The zero-hour recitation discusses the explicitly reviewed general-chemistry problems and assignments of CHEM 1151.

courses.name: Calculus 1 for Science and Engineering
courses.description: Develops differentiation, its scientific applications, and introductory integration.

category_review.locator: MATH 1341 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Limits, differentiation, integration and the fundamental theorem of calculus are the central content.

courses.name: Calculus 2 for Science and Engineering
courses.description: Continues integration methods, series, and introductory vectors and spatial motion.
courses.prerequisites: Additional course-description condition: MATH 1341 or permission of head mathematics advisor.

category_review.locator: MATH 1342 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Integration techniques, infinite series and vectors are the central mathematical topics.

courses.name: Calculus 3 for Science and Engineering
courses.description: Develops multivariable differentiation, multiple integrals and vector calculus.

category_review.locator: MATH 2321 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Multivariable calculus, vector fields and integration theorems are the taught mathematical methods.

courses.name: Differential Equations and Linear Algebra for Engineering
courses.description: Combines differential-equation methods and linear algebra for engineering applications.

category_review.locator: MATH 2341 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Differential equations, numerical methods, transforms and linear algebra are the taught methods, with engineering applications.

courses.name: Probability and Statistics
courses.description: Develops probability distributions and limit theory, then introduces statistical inference.
courses.prerequisites: MATH 1342 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 211M with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1252 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1242 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: MATH 3081 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: Probability distributions, expectation, limit theorems and statistical inference are the core content.

category_review.locator: MATH 3082 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: The recitation explicitly reinforces the reviewed probability/statistics course.

courses.name: Physics for Engineering 1
courses.description: Develops calculus-based mechanics and fluid physics for engineering.
courses.prerequisites: MATH 1241 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1251 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1340 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1341 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 21EM with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1342 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 211M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 2321 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 316M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: PHYS 1151 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course studies Newtonian mechanics, motion, forces, energy and fluids in engineering physics; calculus is a tool for physical problems, not the principal subject.

courses.name: Lab for PHYS 1151
courses.description: Investigates introductory engineering physics through laboratory experiments.

category_review.locator: PHYS 1152 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Experiments accompany PHYS 1151 engineering mechanics and fluids; the laboratory subject is physical science.

courses.name: Interactive Learning Seminar for PHYS 1151
courses.description: Practices mathematical problem solving in mechanics and fluids.

category_review.locator: PHYS 1153 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The seminar solves physical mechanics, equilibrium, dynamics and fluids problems accompanying PHYS 1151; mathematical techniques support those physical models.

courses.name: Introduction to Engineering Co-op Education
courses.description: Prepares engineering students for co-op searches, career planning and global work opportunities.
courses.prerequisites: GE 1000 with a minimum grade of D- or ARCH 1000 with a minimum grade of D- or BIOL 1000 with a minimum grade of D- or BUSN 1102 with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 1000 with a minimum grade of D- or CS 1200 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1000 with a minimum grade of D- or FSEM 1000 with a minimum grade of D- or GENS 1102 with a minimum grade of D- or INPR 1000 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1000 with a minimum grade of D- or PHYS 1000 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: ENCP 2000 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The description centers on employment searches, career management and co-op procedures, without a fixed substantive engineering curriculum.

courses.name: Professional Issues in Engineering
courses.description: Reflects on engineering study and co-op through professional ethics, diversity and career planning.
courses.prerequisites: BIOE 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CHME 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIVE 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or EECE 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or ENCP 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or MEIE 2000 with a minimum grade of D-

category_review.locator: ENCP 3000 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Professional ethics, ethical conflicts, diversity and cultural context are explicit substantive topics, distinguishing this course from generic employment-search preparation.

courses.name: First-Year Seminar
courses.description: Introduces university resources, community participation and academic planning for first-year students.

category_review.locator: GE 1000 course block; description, not department or degree label
category_review.rationale: University transition, support resources and major exploration are orientation, not a fixed technical domain.

courses.name: First-Year Writing
courses.description: Develops research and writing across audiences and genres through workshop practice.

category_review.locator: ENGW 1111 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The workshop teaches rhetorical choices, research-based writing, audience awareness and revision in academic, professional and public communication.

courses.name: Advanced Writing in the Technical Professions
courses.description: Develops research and communication in technical and professional genres.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

category_review.locator: ENGW 3302 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Technical reports, proposals and presentations are the genres used to teach audience analysis, critical research and revision; the subject is technical communication rather than engineering methods.

courses.name: Advanced Writing in the Sciences
courses.description: Develops scientific argument, evidence presentation and research-based writing.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

category_review.locator: ENGW 3307 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: The course analyzes how scientific texts present claims and evidence and teaches scientific writing and revision; quantitative evidence is a communication object, not the primary mathematical subject.

courses.name: Interdisciplinary Advanced Writing in the Disciplines
courses.description: Develops research, revision and writing across disciplinary contexts.
courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C

category_review.locator: ENGW 3315 course block; description and any explicitly accompanying lecture context
category_review.rationale: Interdisciplinary professional, public and academic writing is taught through audience analysis, critical research, peer review and revision.

category_review.locator: GE 1110 official course-description block
category_review.rationale: The description centers on engineering problem formulation, design evaluation, CAD and a technical design project. This is applied engineering design, not an AI method.

category_review.locator: GE 1111 official course-description block
category_review.rationale: The description uses engineering analysis and design problems to teach computation, matrix tools and microcontrollers. Its primary domain practice is engineering problem solving; it is not evidence of an AI specialization.

courses.name: Seminar for CS 1800
courses.description: Reinforces CS 1800 discrete-structures material through seminar discussion, quizzes and assignments.

category_review.locator: CS 1802 seminar description, together with CS 1800 discrete-structures description and reciprocal corequisite conditions
category_review.rationale: The seminar accompanies the explicitly reviewed discrete-structures course and reinforces its mathematical topics through discussion and assignments.

requirements.title: Demonstrating Thought and Action in a Capstone
requirements.summary: Complete at least one designated capstone course in the major. For combined or double majors, the academic units may specify the major for the capstone or allow the student to choose; this policy does not require an extra capstone in every discipline.

requirements.title: NUpath applicability
requirements.summary: Applies to first-year entrants from fall 2016; previously admitted students with another core and transfer students with earlier entry years follow their applicable rules.

requirements.title: Competency-based course eligibility
requirements.summary: Use approved NUpath attributes in course/section listings. Major, minor, concentration or elective coursework can qualify without additional course-level or semester-hour restrictions. Pass/fail and satisfactory/unsatisfactory coursework cannot qualify. This is an eligibility criterion, not an invented extra course pool.

requirements.title: NUpath overlap limits
requirements.summary: One course may fulfill at most 2 of the first eight competencies; writing-intensive-in-major, capstone and experiential attributes can additionally overlap without that cap.

requirements.title: NUpath transfer and examination limits
requirements.summary: Transfer/placement credit may fulfill at most 5 of the first eight competencies using Northeastern course equivalents. Transfer cannot fulfill capstone or experiential requirements; among writing requirements, only first-year writing permits transfer/placement credit.

requirements.title: First-year writing standard
requirements.summary: Complete an approved first-year writing option with C or higher, or qualifying advanced placement/transfer credit. The writing program uses guided self-placement and requires an essay at the first class meeting.

requirements.title: Advanced writing standard
requirements.summary: Complete advanced writing with C or higher. Enrollment requires first-year writing, at least 64 academic semester hours including the enrollment semester, and junior/senior standing. Transfer credit cannot satisfy advanced writing; choose the appropriate program-approved section with advising.

requirements.title: Writing-intensive work in the major
requirements.summary: Complete at least 2 additional writing-intensive major courses, beyond first-year and advanced writing. Approved major courses may also fulfill other NUpath attributes within the overlap rules.

requirements.title: Experiential Learning Graduation Requirement
requirements.summary: Published university policy criteria; apply alongside the concrete program requirements.

requirements.title: Qualifying experiential engagement
requirements.summary: Complete one qualifying university experiential engagement; the concrete program may impose additional or more specific experience requirements.

requirements.title: Co-op
requirements.summary: Complete a qualifying co-op.

requirements.title: Internship
requirements.summary: Complete a qualifying internship.

requirements.title: Clinical placement
requirements.summary: Complete a qualifying clinical placement.

requirements.title: Approved industry-partnership course
requirements.summary: Complete an approved course requiring an industry-partnership project.

requirements.title: Experiential requirement scope
requirements.summary: The standard U.S.-campus matriculated degree rule applies to these Boston degree programs. Published exceptions cover nondegree, CPS undergraduate, online/primarily online, PhD and certificate programs, continuing Mills/Marymount Manhattan students, and London dual-degree students; assess any individual exception against that policy.

requirements.title: Graduation Requirements
requirements.summary: Published university policy criteria; apply alongside the concrete program requirements.

requirements.title: Graduation and diploma clearance
requirements.summary: Meet academic, program, experiential and residency requirements and remain in good standing. Clear financial, experiential-education and disciplinary deficiencies before diploma receipt; the college advising office reviews the degree audit.

requirements.title: Coursework after matriculation
requirements.summary: Complete degree coursework at Northeastern, an entity with a formal contractual/consortial/partnership relationship, or approved Northeastern study abroad. Taking another accredited institution’s course requires a college petition under the published exceptions.

requirements.title: Graduation application
requirements.summary: Submit the graduation application by the published deadlines to receive the diploma, including when not attending the optional ceremony.

requirements.title: Degrees, Majors, and Minors
requirements.summary: Published university policy criteria; apply alongside the concrete program requirements.

requirements.title: Combined-major discipline and integration criteria
requirements.summary: The combined major includes at least 9 courses from each participating discipline, at most 2 courses counting in both, and at least 16 courses overall, with multiple curricular integration points. These are program-design/fulfillment criteria, not additional courses to add to the published degree plan.

requirements.title: Designated home college
requirements.summary: A designated home college registers and graduates the student; most combined majors allow a home-college choice. Catalog hosting context does not establish an individual student’s choice. Apply that college’s published rules and approved program of study.

requirements.title: Combined-major award identity
requirements.summary: Completion earns one major, one degree and one diploma; the combined major and home college appear on transcript and diploma. Preserve this concrete program’s BSChE designation.

requirements.title: Academic Progression Standards
requirements.summary: Published university policy criteria; apply alongside the concrete program requirements.

requirements.title: University academic standing
requirements.summary: Maintain overall GPA 1.800 at each first-year semester end and cumulative GPA 2.000 thereafter; earn at least 12 semester hours in the completed semester. Individual colleges/programs may add progression criteria.

requirements.title: Incomplete grades and probation
requirements.summary: When pending incomplete credits leave a student below full-time status, GPA determines temporary probation until the incomplete is resolved. Full-time students missing good-standing criteria are placed on academic probation for the following semester.

requirements.title: Dismissal and appeal policy
requirements.summary: Two full-term semesters of continuing probation may lead to dismissal. A GPA below 1.000 or fewer than four earned hours in a semester or cumulatively may also trigger college-discretionary dismissal; pending incompletes are excluded. Students may appeal to their college Academic Standing Committee. A probation appeal generally allows no more than 1 additional full-term academic semester to regain good standing.

requirements.title: Major declaration deadline
requirements.summary: Declare a major no later than the end of the sophomore year; declaration may occur on admission. This is a timing criterion, not another course requirement.

requirements.title: Conditional major-change eligibility
requirements.summary: For a full-time undergraduate changing major, meet the receiving major’s immediate-entry criteria, or have cumulative GPA 2.000 or higher and satisfy its transition criteria. A lower GPA requires receiving-major discretion. These are conditional admission rules, not additional obligations for every student already in the degree.

requirements.title: Conditional major-change advising and procedure
requirements.summary: Discuss a proposed change in person with the receiving-major advisor, who certifies immediate entry or arranges a transition term. Review success and completion timing; published receiving-unit transition criteria, any required audition/portfolio and deadlines still apply. International students must inform the Office of Global Services of a change. No immigration eligibility is inferred from this academic policy.

requirements.title: Conditional concentration catalog-year consistency
requirements.summary: If pursuing a concentration, use the same catalog year as the major. A later-introduced concentration requires adopting both that later major and concentration curriculum; students retaining an earlier major catalog may select only concentrations offered in that year. This does not make a concentration mandatory where the concrete degree does not require one.
